quote_text:
Perfect. Okay, everyone, if you just raise your  hand if you have got a question for Thomas,  
and please use the microphone available.  If you go first, second. Let’s go. Thomas,  
obviously a victory that you guys were looking at  and a victory to close out going into the World  
Cup. Mike Remy with WESH, the NBC station here  in Orlando. I just wanted to get your overall  
reactions today with the fans that came out here  to watch the national team in Orlando, and your  
impressions overall on the stadium, the pitch and  the facilities. Nice stadium, nice little stadium,  
good football stadium and a good atmosphere. I  think the team did a lot to get the energy going  
and there was a beautiful connection between our  team and the fans. It was amazing conditions. In  
hindsight, it was good for us to have a bit of a  delay so we could even adapt to that and see if  
it affected us. The group was amazing. We were not  distracted, we did not lose our focus and we had  
an excellent and determined performance from start  to finish. Is that one of the things that you have  
got to prepare for, the impact of the rain delays?  Also, just after the hydration breaks, there have  
been a couple of attacks for New Zealand and Costa  Rica. Is that something you have to focus on,  
the concentration after those hydration breaks? I  am not aware of that, to be honest. I have to look  
at it again. I did not feel any dangerous moments  today. It is just football. We play against strong  
and physical teams, like today. Very physical for  a long, long period and it took time to open up  
and tire them, and open up the gaps. But there is  no focus at the moment for after breaks. I did not  
realise that this is an issue and I struggle  to prepare for things that we do not know if  
they are coming. So what should we prepare for? A  half-an-hour break? For a delay at the start? For  
a delay in the middle? We just know that things  can come and we know how we want to react. Calm,  
focused and relaxed, and we want to focus on  the stuff that we can influence. We did this  
today on a high level. That is why I am very  happy. Hi, Thomas. There seemed to be a little  
bit of confusion with the penalty in the second  half. I think Jude had the ball and then there  
was some kind of discussion with the bench  and Anthony ended up taking it. Can you just  
run us through what happened there? Just a lot of  substitutions and then it was not clear anymore,  
the order of the takers. Anthony was the second  taker and it was not on the wall. Normally it is  
on the wall because we know, of course, we only  have five substitutes. A lot of substitutions. So  
we had a bit of a miscommunication, but it was our  responsibility and so we needed to do it verbally.  
No problem. Thomas, I know you said to TV you  were very happy with the overall team performance,  
very happy with the guys that came on in the  second half, but compared to the other day, Gordon  
and Bellingham seemed to really give you an extra  dimension going forward. Can you just talk about  
those two performances? No, I do not want to talk  about the two performances because, for me, it is  
absolutely too short to focus on these two guys.  We had a very strong team from the beginning.  
We knew that and we had strong substitutes  because that is the nature of the team, and the  
attitude from the bench was top. I just liked the  performance over the 90 minutes and both players,  
Jude and Anthony, were a part of it. But for me,  this is a high-level team performance on and off  
the ball, counter-pressing and ball wins. The guys  who finished this game off were very strong. The  
guys who came off were ready to push from the  side. Very good, very good test and, for sure,  
a team effort, not individual. More broadly, are  you exactly where you want to be in the last game?  
I wished for that. I demanded that. I said it  before the match. We want to push it to the next  
level from intensity, commitment and cohesion,  and we did that. You could see the impact of  
the Arsenal players coming into camp and you could  see also the impact of training. Of course, we see  
the adaptation to the heat, we see the adaptation  to the climate and we see things clicking. But we  
demanded it today from the players to take a next  step and they did. That was what we wished for and  
the players delivered, and I am proud of them, how  they did it. Anyway, the most important is how we  
play and the result then takes care of itself. But  we did it on a high level and for this moment it  
was very good to almost end the prep camp like  this. We have tomorrow another training session  
and another in-house game to give the guys some  minutes who did not play so much. If we do not  
have any injuries and get a good performance  out of that, then we have what we wished for.  
Hi, Thomas. I just wanted to ask you about the  next couple of days, really. You have got that  
behind-closed-doors game and then, I do not  know, is it a day off on Friday before you  
go? Talk about what you want for the next 48 hours  exactly. That we get some minutes into the legs,  
and game minutes, not training minutes, but game  minutes, for the three players who did not play,  
for the guys who came maybe just for 22 plus  extra time. So we can manage that. We can manage  
the game time tomorrow. It will be very likely not  more than, I do not know, two times 30 minutes or  
something like this. And then the players get  one and a half days off, not only physically,  
but also to switch off, and well-deservedly.  Then we start the next chunk of the tournament,  
which is the group stage, and we change location,  which I am looking forward to. Not because we  
did not like it. It was excellent here and,  until today, on the highest level. But it is  
nice to change scenery and to give it a new  frame for the next period of the tournament,  
which is then the group stage. Thomas, I know you  do not want to talk about individuals, but does  
how many times Jude wins the ball in the first 10  minutes give him the platform to go on and do what  
he does for the rest of the game with the ball? I  think the energy off the ball set the tone today,  
and we made this also very clear before the  match because we trained a lot of offensive  
solutions. But we made very clear that the DNA  of us is also off the ball and the work rate,  
which gives us a good feeling and gives us the  chance to impose ourselves on the opponent. The  
movement is up front and not running backwards.  That made us strong in qualification football.  
I wanted to see Jude in the combination today for  the first time with Harvey Elliott and Declan in  
the centre of the game. I know what Morgan gives  us there. I just saw it so many times. It was the  
first time for Jude and he buys into these ideas.  He has to and he loves to do it. That is part of  
our game and he did it, like everyone else, on  a high level. Thomas, hi. There were a couple of  
occasions when Dan Burn and Jude Bellingham were  trying to get to corners and they were stopped.  
When is this rule on grappling going to actually  come into play? Very good question. I have no  
answer for that. Does it actually help? You have  got 20 games to watch before you play, so you can  
actually see whether there is any consistency.  It will be difficult to have consistency. I think  
it will be very difficult. To give credit  to the referees and to VAR and everything,  
it will be very, very difficult to hold a  consistent line. It is not difficult to preview  
situations that are whistled in one match and not  whistled in the other, or they are whistled in a  
direction where you think, was this more a foul  of the defender or more of the striker? And yeah,  
this is what is coming. There are some new rules  and new rules shortly before the tournament. Yeah,  
that is what can happen. Even then, I think we  will be strong in set pieces. That is the nature  
of us and we want to be strong in set pieces.  We are strong already and we will get stronger  
because the group is ready to dig in and just  learn in meetings and on the training pitch,  
which is not the most attractive training session,  to train set pieces. But they are just willing to  
do it because they have a dream and they know that  it takes invisible work and it takes work that  
is repetitive. It takes work that is maybe not so  nice to do and they are ready to do it. So we want  
to be a strong set-piece team and then we adapt  to what is allowed and what is not allowed. Hi,  
Thomas. It does seem like the camp has gone really  well, whether it be camaraderie or adaptation to  
the heat. I was just wondering how you are finding  adapting to coaching in tournaments. This is very  
different from anything you have done. Yeah,  I had a feeling, and I had more until now,  
it was more the feeling of a pre-season, like an  overseas pre-season, and it was good like this. I  
think it is enough if the pressure and tournament  pressure comes a bit later, because it will come.  
The tension will come naturally. I think we set  the tone today in the meeting and the players  
were ready to follow, to have, like I said,  a next step in intensity and the way we play,  
to push ourselves and get a good feeling out of  it, which we absolutely did. I felt today the  
energy in the stadium, amazing. I thought, okay,  if we can really play like this and grow into the  
tournament, and have this kind of cohesion and  brotherhood and team spirit that we showed today,  
then we will have an amazing connection with  the fans and this will hopefully be an amazing  
experience. Because, like you said, it is the  first time for me and it is a World Cup, and it is  
coming. I think once the ball is rolling and games  are already there, then I will feel it. The latest  
in Kansas, when we prepare the official match, the  tension will grow. But normally that is the stuff  
that I personally enjoy the most, and then you  feel that you are alive. Thank you, guys. Thanks.
